title: The Keening
summary: The holy sound that rose from Mecca in the Prophet’s time.

claims.text: As Muhammad embraced the role of Prophet, a sound heard only by Cainites began to spread from Mecca across Arabia.
It began as a faint whisper at dusk and swelled to a roar by noon, stealing Cainite sleep and wearing at their sanity.
It grew stronger the nearer a vampire came to Mecca, and any Cainite who entered the city was consumed in blinding white flame.
Devout Muslim Cainites such as Suleiman endured it gladly as a sign of devotion to God.
Followers of the Road of the Nomad meet every challenge directly with courage and cunning, shun lavish havens, servants and ghouls, and prefer a wanderer’s nights.
They are decisive to the point of impulse; cowardice is despised, though deception that succeeds is respected.
Its sins run from choosing reason over instinct at the highest ratings, through owning more than one can carry and keeping a permanent lair, to breaking one’s word or refusing a challenge.

title: Tariq el-Shaitan
summary: The Road of the Devil among Islamic Cainites.

claims.text: Followers revel in what their society forbids and try to corrupt the virtues of those around them with gifts and sweet words.
A few go further, into outright devil worship; this is the variant held by elder Baali, who revere the Children.
Its Virtues are Conviction, Instinct and Courage, and followers seldom hide their taste for luxury, though Ashirra zeal makes open degeneracy dangerous.
Many of the Embraced cannot keep their faith in Heaven and Hell, whether through bitterness or because immortality makes an afterlife seem pointless.
The Road of Community offers such Cainites a path of belonging instead.
Religious Prohibition is a Flaw for a Cainite who kept the faith: at 2 points the vampire feeds only on animals or blood drained by a ritual butcher.
At 4 points the vampire feeds only in real need, with a blood pool of three or less, and may sink into self-loathing for nights afterwards.
Outspoken Dhimmi, a 4-point Flaw, marks a Jew or Christian who openly champions that faith against the sharia and risks punishment.

title: Hedayat Iman, the Gifts of Faith

claims.text: An Ashirra must study with a teacher who knows a power or ritual, through prayer and inward focus taking days for a first-level power and years for a fifth-level ritual, and cannot learn one rated above Theology.
Prayer is the centre of every Hedayat Iman power; the path is used mainly by the Haji, and only by them after the Mongol invasion.

Saut Allah, the Voice of God, has the caster lead others in prayer toward Mecca for at least an hour, then spend a blood point and roll Charisma + Leadership at difficulty 7, less one per hour of prayer.
Each success grants one listener a temporary Willpower point until dawn, never the caster; a botch costs each listener a Willpower point.

title: The Muslim dead of the Shadowlands

claims.text: Many devout Muslim ghosts are horrified that the afterlife is a wretched shadow of the living world and not the Paradise promised.
The atheist European Stygian empire rules these lands, and Charon lets Christian ghosts travel the Byways freely between Necropoli.

Many Muslim dead join the Renegades; a few, led by al-Alam, who died a martyr defending Jerusalem from the crusaders, aim to drive the Stygian Legionnaires from the Jerusalem Necropolis and found a Muslim kingdom of the dead.
